records.title: Doha reports investment talks in California
records.body: Qatar’s trade ministry identifies talks with US, Singaporean, South Korean, British and Indian officials and meetings with Mubadala, Alphabet, Temasek and Scale AI. Its account identifies participants and investment discussions. It reports no transaction value or signed project.
records.source: Qatar, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
records.section: Minister of State for Foreign Trade Participates in the Signing, final five paragraphs

records.title: Marcos clarifies the proposed Philippine site
records.body: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. said in Shenzhen that the proposed AI industrial development would exclude data centres and that the site agreement remained unsigned. This narrows the publicly stated scope. A signed framework and an agreed site plan remain the next evidence to track.
records.section: Kapihan with the media in Shenzhen, exchange on Pax Silica

records.title: Japan publishes the multilateral roster
records.body: Japan’s foreign ministry lists 25 countries and the European Union as declaration signatories. It reports that 15 delegations attended the November retreat. The wider declaration roster, attendance list and ten signatures on the San Francisco text measure different forms of participation.
records.section: Participation in the Pax Silica Founders Retreat, Reference 1

records.title: Ten governments sign the San Francisco Declaration
records.body: Australia, India, Israel, Japan, Qatar, Singapore, South Korea, the UAE, the UK and the US signed the separate declaration. They agreed to establish working groups. Their definition of critical infrastructure covers ports, logistics networks, energy systems and the digital platforms that coordinate them.
records.source: Australia, Department of Industry, Science and Resources
records.section: Introduction, signatory list. Declaration, working groups and Second

records.title: Manila awaits Washington’s response on the zone
records.body: The Philippine presidency reported that the Bases Conversion and Development Authority had received guidance for negotiations. Officials were awaiting a US response to the draft framework. The outstanding instrument concerns the industrial zone, distinct from Philippine participation in the multilateral declaration.
records.section: Malacañang press briefing, Sam Medenilla’s question on the draft framework

records.title: Paraguay becomes the 26th signatory
records.body: Foreign Minister Rubén Ramírez Lezcano signed in Washington. Paraguay tied its participation to the possible use of its hydropower and minerals in AI infrastructure in the Americas.
records.section: Paraguay se suma a la Declaración de Pax Silica, paras. 1 to 3

records.title: Silicon Highway funding call opens
records.body: Federal opportunity DFOP0019193 sought proposals for a platform to verify cargo provenance and expedite compliance along participating supply chains. The solicitation anticipated three cooperative agreements, with individual awards from US$1 million to US$50 million. Applications closed on 20 August. The listing names no award recipients.
records.source: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Economic and Business Affairs
records.section: Award details, Important dates and Summary

records.title: Italy joins Pax Silica
records.body: Italy’s foreign ministry dates accession to 31 July. It subsequently linked Italy’s bilateral critical minerals working group with the United States to that decision.
records.source: Italy, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
records.section: Tajani and Rubio sign the Memorandum of Understanding, paragraph on accession

records.title: Doha reports signature of the AI Opportunity statement
records.body: Qatar’s trade ministry reported that its minister had signed a joint statement on AI with the United States during the Washington summit. The ministry describes the statement as an annex to Qatar’s January declaration. The date shown here is the ministry’s publication date.
records.source: Qatar Ministry of Commerce and Industry
records.section: Minister of State for Foreign Trade Affairs Participates in Pax Silica Summit, para. 3

records.title: Washington summit closes with 24 signatories
records.body: The State Department reported ten additional signatories at the second summit on 25 and 26 June. Private firms and affiliate governments also attended. Attendance alone did not confer signatory status.
records.source: U.S. Department of State, distributed media note
records.section: United States Hosts Second Pax Silica Summit, paras. 1 to 3

records.title: European Commission confirms EU signature
records.body: The Commission signed on behalf of the European Union. The EU has its own entry in the declaration roster alongside those EU member governments that signed individually.
records.section: Commission signs Pax Silica declaration, opening paragraph

records.title: Kazakhstan signs two instruments
records.body: Kazakhstan signed the Pax Silica accession declaration and an AI Opportunity Partnership statement in Washington. Its embassy identified domestic mineral processing as a prospective area of cooperation.
records.section: Kazakhstan Joins the Pax Silica Initiative, paras. 1, 2 and 8

records.title: Norway announces accession
records.body: Norway’s government identified fourteen participants and named Ambassador Anniken Huitfeldt as its signatory. It placed access to advanced technology markets among its reasons for joining.
records.source: Norway, Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Fisheries
records.section: Norway Joins the Pax Silica Initiative, paras. 2 and 6 to 7

records.title: Finland signs in Washington
records.body: Economic Affairs Minister Sakari Puisto signed for Finland. The government highlighted network connectivity alongside chip production, mineral inputs and power supply.
records.section: Finland to participate, paras. 1 and 5

records.title: Philippines signs the declaration
records.body: The Philippine Board of Investments publishes the signed instrument alongside a separate letter proposing an industrial hub and a separate AI Opportunity Partnership statement.
records.section: Downloads, Pax Silica Declaration PH-US signed 04-16-26

records.title: Washington and Manila propose an economic security zone
records.body: The two governments announced plans for an industrial zone of approximately 4,000 acres in the Philippines. The April announcement establishes the scale of the proposal. Land transfer, financial close and construction each require separate evidence.
records.section: U.S. and Philippines Plan the Launch of Historic 4,000-Acre Economic Security Zone

records.title: Washington proposes a $250 million Pax Silica Fund
records.body: The State Department proposed working with Congress to allocate US$250 million in foreign assistance to minerals extraction and processing, infrastructure and semiconductor-related manufacturing. It sought additional sovereign and private capital. The figure describes the proposed US allocation. The announcement gives no amount disbursed.
records.section: Department of State Launches Pax Silica Fund, paras. 1 to 3

records.title: Sweden signs in Houston
records.body: Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard signed the declaration. Sweden identified connectivity, minerals, chips and energy as sectors where the partners could combine industrial capacity.
records.section: Sweden joins Pax Silica initiative, paras. 1 and 4

records.title: India joins at the AI Impact Summit
records.body: India announced its accession on the fifth day of the summit. Its electronics ministry linked cooperation on mineral inputs and chip fabrication to the infrastructure needed to deploy AI.
records.source: India, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
records.section: India Joins Pax Silica, paras. 1 and 2

records.title: The United Arab Emirates joins
records.body: Minister of State Saeed bin Mubarak Al Hajeri signed for the UAE alongside U.S. Under Secretary Jacob Helberg.
records.source: United Arab Emirates, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
records.section: UAE accession announcement, paras. 1 and 2 (Arabic)

records.title: Qatar signs in Doha
records.body: Qatar joined the declaration through a bilateral signing with the United States. Its commerce ministry identified safeguarding technology inputs and improving supply continuity as priorities.
records.source: Qatar, Ministry of Commerce and Industry
records.section: Qatar and the United States Sign, paras. 1 and 2

records.title: Seven governments sign in Washington
records.body: Australia, Israel, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, the United Kingdom and the United States signed at the inaugural summit. The U.S. State Department convened the meeting to address economic security across AI supply chains.
records.section: Participation of Senior Deputy Minister Akahori, paras. 1 and 2

records.title: Green Mining and Minerals Initiative
records.body: China and partners proposed cooperation on minerals trade, investment, technology and local benefits at the Johannesburg G20 summit. Its overlap with Pax Silica concerns who finances processing and on what terms. The announcement establishes a proposal, not a mine or financing commitment.
records.section: Johannesburg summit announcement, paragraphs 1 to 3

records.title: Global AI Governance Action Plan
records.body: The Shanghai plan calls for interoperable computing infrastructure, common standards and cooperation on power, networks and data centres. It offers a competing policy vision for access to compute. Adoption or procurement needs separate evidence in each jurisdiction.
records.source: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of China
records.section: Action 4, Accelerating digital infrastructure construction

records.title: Digital Silk Road
records.body: China’s 2023 white paper records bilateral digital cooperation agreements and work on subsea and terrestrial cables. These networks offer a comparison where governments choose connectivity partners. A claim of competing bids requires a named procurement.
records.source: State Council Information Office of China
records.section: Part III, §6, Digital silk road cooperation

records.title: Global Gateway
records.body: The EU launched a financing strategy for digital, energy and transport connections. Its original €300 billion figure was a mobilisation target for 2021 to 2027. Compare individual projects for overlap or co-financing before inferring a rivalry.
records.section: Launch announcement, opening two paragraphs
